before.headline: Brixton used more electricity because cold weather and a one-off day raised consumption while wholesale prices and a drop in wind generation pushed up the unit cost.
sentences: The bill rose by £104.67 (15.5%) driven mainly by a 55.3% increase from higher wholesale prices.
Cold weather added £37.32 to the bill, making up a large part of the £45.80 volume effect.
A single unusual day accounted for 31.0% of the total bill change.
Electricity used grew by 179 kWh (6.9%) from 2,594 kWh to 2,773 kWh.
The average unit price paid rose from 25.6 p/kWh to 27.7 p/kWh as the wind share of generation fell by −3.1 pp.
ruledOut: H5: Timing shift changed the bill by only £1.03, so it is not a cause.
H11: No day deviated far from expected use (largest distance 2.6 sd), so it is not a cause.
H7: Meter checks found 0 faults across 1 site.
H9: No missing or extra half-hours in 2 site-windows checked (1,344 slots expected).
